title: Premium stabilization can preserve enrollment while shifting risk and leaving the causal effect open
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office review of CMS's 2025 Medicare Part D Premium Stabilization Demonstration
geography: United States Medicare Part D standalone prescription-drug plans; 2024-2025 with demonstration cost estimates for 2025-2026

observations.period: 2024-2025; standalone Part D plans without low-income subsidy beneficiaries

denominator.unit: CMS-weighted beneficiaries in standalone Part D plans who were not eligible for the low-income subsidy

projected_no_demo_premium.value: average monthly premium would have nearly doubled if beneficiaries stayed in their 2024 plan; 37% would have faced increases over $40

observed_average_premium.value: increased from $42 in 2024 to $43 in 2025 under the demonstration

enrollment.value: increased 2% from 2024 to 2025; standalone plans remained 42% of all Part D enrollment

observations.method: GAO analysis of CMS premium and enrollment data, review of demonstration documents, and interviews with CMS, ASPE, plan sponsors, and beneficiary organizations.
observations.uncertainty: The projected no-demonstration premium is a modeled comparison, and observed premium and enrollment changes may reflect other Part D benefit changes; a causal evaluation remains necessary.
observations.subgroup: Beneficiaries in standalone Part D plans who were not eligible for the low-income subsidy and therefore paid plan premiums.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable premiums and enrollment can indicate meaningful protection even without a completed causal evaluation; other plan or benefit changes may also have contributed.

beneficiary_reduction.value: CMS reduced beneficiary premiums by up to $15 in 2025 and limited plan increases to $35

federal_cost.unit: dollars estimated for the demonstration in 2025 and 2026

risk_shift.value: Medicare subsidized premiums and provided additional protection to plan sponsors

medication_access.value: disruption to medication access was a projected risk from enrollment changes, not an observed outcome in this review

observations.method: GAO review of CMS implementation documents, cost estimates, and evaluation plans.
observations.uncertainty: The estimate does not show net public cost after avoided medical spending, nor does it establish medication adherence or health effects.
observations.subgroup: Medicare beneficiaries, plan sponsors, and federal taxpayers affected by standalone Part D premium stabilization.
observations.counterinterpretation: Public risk-taking may be justified if it prevents harmful plan switching or medication disruption; that tradeoff requires the planned evaluation.

boundary: This record measures projected and observed Part D premiums, enrollment, demonstration rules, and estimated public cost. It does not establish medication adherence, health outcomes, household net relief, plan quality, or the demonstration's isolated causal effect.
